newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares recover at close, paper stocks well bid.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares recover at close, paper stocks well bid.

text.p: * NZ shares ease, Telecom tests lower and finds support
* Brokers report moderate volume after quiet start
* Unsatisfied demand noted for paper/pulp stocks
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -7.37 at 2,349.43
348 nil * NZSC cap index -12.57 at 5,037.33
336 nil * NZMC .NZMC cap index -12.39 at 1,868.07 365 -15 * Volume NZ$64 million. Futures, -1 at 1185
695 -2 * Other movers - +25 -15
New Zealand shares closed lower on Tuesday, but found renewed support in afternoon trading, brokers said.
The NZSE40 Capital Index ended the day 7.37 points off at 2349.43.
Turnover was a moderate $64 million including $14.9 million in Telecom, which found some support at the close although there was still some stock overhanging the market, brokers said.
"It was a lot weaker earlier on, but found some renewed buying in afternoon trade," Luke Koekoek of brokers J B Were and Son said.

"The stocks that bounced the most were Telecom, which hit $6.91 earlier but found some solid buying up to $6.95, and the paper stocks again saw moderate turnover and unsatisfied demand around the close," Koekoek said.
The company confirmed after the close that it had been buying in the market at between $6.91 and $7.00 during the day.
Koekoek said while the paper stocks were steady on the day they were well bid at the close.
Carter Holt Harvey finished level at $3.48 and Fletcher Paper was also steady at $3.36.
Fletcher Energy was the big mover of the day rising 20 cents to $4.85 after peaking at $4.90.
Rights to Infratil International closed their first day's trading at 5.2 cents on turnover of two million shares.
Koekoek said the outlook for the market was for a further easing on Wednesday.

"I would think it will ease off a little bit because the market has had a pretty good run. I suppose one of the features in the short term might be these paper stocks which still look as if there is a bit of buying around," he said.
